- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts tend to be too low in the first 5–10 days, then gradually rise — suggesting a lag in capturing recent price momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., 70+), model forecasts often overshoot or fail to peak accurately, underestimating the magnitude of the spike.
- Model shows weak mean reversion — fails to anticipate sharp reversals or corrections after peaks.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the early days, especially when historical prices are trending upward.
- Model exhibits a persistent bias toward lower values, particularly when true outcomes are above 70 — suggesting underweighting of bullish signals.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are systematically too low, especially in the first 10 days, then improve — indicating a delayed adjustment to recent trends.
- Model fails to capture the “late-stage” price acceleration — often underestimates the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon.
